title: Snowflake Cortex Pricing: AI Credit Costs in 2026
summary: Snowflake Cortex pricing costs $2.00 to $2.20 per AI credit depending on region. You can calculate the expected bill for your workloads based on location.
body_markdown:
## Set up a weekly Cortex spend check with Activepieces


Catch a runaway bill within days with a five-step Activepieces workflow that reads last week's credits and messages you when they pass your limit.


That suits you if you stay on Cortex rather than buying an outside platform.


Activepieces runs a chain of steps on a schedule from an MIT-licensed core, with 747 integrations to wire them together, Snowflake among them, and no code needed, allowing you to connect Snowflake with hundreds of other services without writing code.


Do nothing and you find out at invoice time, after a badly aimed query has already run all month. The five steps below are the whole job:


1. Add a Schedule trigger set for Monday morning.
2. Connect the Snowflake integration with a login that can read account usage.
3. Run a query against the account usage views for last week's Cortex credits.
4. Add a condition that compares the total to your limit.
5. Send the result to Slack or email.


Read the workflow top to bottom and each step is one block on the canvas, so someone who has never written code can follow it. The three stages below group them by what you decide at each point.


Pick the Schedule trigger, choose weekly, and set Monday at 08:00 in your own time zone. Monday morning means the previous week is complete and the alert lands before anyone starts new experiments.


Check the time zone setting, because a default you didn't choose can shift the cutoff and split a day's usage across two reports.


### Stage 2: Query last week's Cortex credits


Add the Snowflake integration and sign in with a role that can read the account usage schema, nothing broader. That limits the damage if the connection details ever leak.


Then add a query step that sums Cortex credits from the account usage views over the past seven days.


Because the account usage views trail real time, Monday morning is a sensible read point, but a spike from Sunday night may be only partly counted.


Group the result by service, and ideally by user or warehouse, so the alert names the culprit rather than just a total.


Since warehouse and search usage sit in neighbouring views you can sum the same way, the charges around the AI calls show up here too.


### Stage 3: Alert when the total passes your limit


Add a condition that continues only when the weekly total is above your limit. Set the limit from your credit rate and edition price, so the alert reads as dollars you would actually mind.


Then add a Slack or email step that sends the total, the top spender and a link to the usage page.


If you want a quiet week to produce no message, leave the condition as it is. If you want proof the check is still running, add a short "all clear" branch.


Some of this you get already from Snowflake's own budgets, which can notify you when spend crosses a threshold you set inside the account.


The workflow adds a fixed weekly rhythm and a breakdown in a channel your team already reads. The two together cost little and close most of the gap between a surprise and a decision.
